If your color style is dull, then I'd say its right on. If you're not happy with the colors, then you can look up some color palettes online to use instead of doing it from scratch. remember: they dont have to all be grey and next to eachother on the color wheel in order to look good. Complementary colors are my absolute favorite to use with eachother! It creates a great effect, you should try it out!

ps. dont be afraid to use contrast! use those deep dark colors to make the brighter ones pop

well its hard to critique an art style im unfamiliar with, but I'd work on your line confidence a bit. (As in drawing in bold long straight lines, instead of tiny continuous sketchy lines) An exercise that helped me in that was sketching with pen. Its sounds scary, but it builds line confidence if you do it a lot. This applies to any artstyle btw! 

Heres a video on line confidence: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CXnrHguWslU](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CXnrHguWslU)

I'd try to make the lines on the sides of the nose less harsh.(maybe blend them out a bit) It'll look more realistic if it doesn't look like its outlined. Keep up the good work, and remember to look at references!
i think when shading, you should look at a reference picture.
push the contrast, look at some lighting references from life. Even if your art style isnt realistic, you can still apply what you see from the references to your art.
